newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankgesellschaft 96 profit slumps, sees improvement.
newsitem.headline: Bankgesellschaft 96 profit slumps, sees improvement.

text.p: Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG, the state-owned German bank, on Friday reported a slump in net profit to 47 million marks ($27.3 million) in 1996 from 476 million in the year earlier due to a sharp rise in risk provisions.
But Bankgesellschaft, Germany's sixth largest listed bank, said it was keeping its dividend unchanged at 1.10 marks because it expected earnings to stabilise in 1997.
Bankgesellschaft said 1996 earnings were affected by a sharp rise in the need for loan loss provisions.
The bank had announced last December it was setting aside 2.2 billion marks in its 1996 accounts to cover problem loans amid an economic slump in its home region of Berlin and east Germany.
Operating profit after risk provisions fell to 355 million marks from 958 million marks. Before risk provisions, operating profit totalled 1.78 billion marks, up 5.6 percent, the bank said.
The group balance sheet total rose 19.9 percent to 337.5 billion marks.
